# SYMBOLS.md -- exported-symbol parity (`nm -D`)

Generated by `gen_symbols.sh`.  The C build produces three shared objects:

* `app/libsphincs_core_det.so` -- core (`address.c fors.c merkle.c sign.c utils.c`
  `utilsx1.c wots.c wotsx1.c`) **+ `rng.c`** (NIST AES-256-CTR-DRBG `randombytes`)
* `app/libsphincs_core.so`     -- the same core **+ `randombytes.c`** (`/dev/urandom`)
* `lib/<backend>/lib<backend>.so` -- the selected hash backend + `thash_<backend>_<THASH>.c`
  (+ a second copy of `utils.c` for blake/sha2)

The Rust crate builds **one** cdylib, `libsphincs_core_det.so`, which therefore has
to export the union of `libsphincs_core_det.so` and `lib<backend>.so`.
`libsphincs_core.so` adds no new symbol names (its `randombytes` is the same name
with the `randombytes.c` body; the deterministic variant is the one the Rust `[lib]`
name selects, so `rng.c`'s `randombytes` is the one that is exported).

## Rust-only extra exports

`nm -D` on the Rust cdylib is a strict superset of the C union.  The only
configuration where it is a *proper* superset is the shake backend, where the
Rust port supplies the 15 entry points that `lib/shake/include/fips202.h`
declares but `lib/shake/src/fips202.c` never defines:

```
shake128 shake128_absorb shake128_squeezeblocks
shake128_inc_init shake128_inc_absorb shake128_inc_finalize shake128_inc_squeeze
sha3_256 sha3_256_inc_init sha3_256_inc_absorb sha3_256_inc_finalize
sha3_512 sha3_512_inc_init sha3_512_inc_absorb sha3_512_inc_finalize
```

They have no C counterpart, so they cannot be differentially tested; see the
note at the end of `CONFIGS.md`.  Symbol parity (C ⊆ Rust) is unaffected.

## `libsphincs_core.so` vs `libsphincs_core_det.so`

The only difference is which `randombytes` implementation is linked:

| | `randombytes` |
|---|---|
| `libsphincs_core_det.so` (`rng.c`) | `int randombytes(unsigned char*, unsigned long long)` -- AES-256-CTR-DRBG, deterministic, also exports `randombytes_init`, `seedexpander`, `seedexpander_init`, `AES256_CTR_DRBG_Update`, `AES256_ECB`, `DRBG_ctx` |
| `libsphincs_core.so` (`randombytes.c`) | `void randombytes(unsigned char*, unsigned long long)` -- reads `/dev/urandom` |

The Rust `[lib] name = "sphincs_core_det"` selects the deterministic variant,
so `rng.rs` owns the exported `randombytes`; `randombytes.rs` is the translation
of the `/dev/urandom` variant and is deliberately **not** `#[no_mangle]`
(exporting it would collide).  This introduces no missing symbol: the *name*
`randombytes` is exported either way.
